note: Principle library for Teamwork. 'forces' come from the website's Path to Agency cards (Matthew Schmidt/index.html, ideaData). 'cases' are the thirty Module 3 management cases from Decision OS (decision-os/js/scenarios3.js); 'lens' and 'tension' name the book each lesson draws on. 'habits' are Module 3's habit families. Book-derived lines are the author of Decision OS's own readings of the books, not quotations. Status of every entry: synthesis.

books.CEO: What the CEO Wants You to Know

before_questions: Am I trying to solve the problem, or prove that I'm right?
What am I avoiding saying because it's uncomfortable?
What part of this have I contributed to?
Am I confusing accountability with punishment?
Can I hold a high standard and genuinely want this person to succeed?

awareness.name: Awareness
awareness.healthy: People examine their own assumptions and contribution before diagnosing others.
awareness.warning: Blame increases. Defensiveness increases. The same problem keeps happening despite repeated attempts to fix other people.
awareness.pattern: The organization is treating problems as something other people have rather than something the system is producing.
awareness.move: Before solving the problem, examine your own role in creating or maintaining it.
awareness.ask: What might I be contributing that I can't currently see?

trust.name: Trust
trust.tag: Create the conditions for people to do their best work.
trust.healthy: People tell the truth, ask for help, challenge ideas, take risks, and recover from mistakes.
trust.warning: People stay quiet in meetings. Problems surface late. Everyone agrees publicly and disagrees privately.
trust.pattern: People are managing their relationship with authority rather than focusing entirely on the work.
trust.move: Reward candor, especially when the information is uncomfortable.
trust.ask: What truth are people least likely to tell me?

conditions.name: Conditions
conditions.tag: Design the environment, not just the behavior.
conditions.healthy: The environment makes the desired behavior relatively easy and the right priorities visible.
conditions.warning: People are constantly told to communicate better, take ownership, or prioritize, but the system keeps producing the opposite.
conditions.pattern: The organization is trying to change people without changing the conditions around them.
conditions.move: Change the environment that produces the behavior.
conditions.ask: What are our current conditions making almost inevitable?

value.name: Value
value.healthy: People understand who they serve, what matters to them, and how their work contributes to the outcome.
value.warning: More activity, more meetings, more reports, but little movement in meaningful outcomes.
value.pattern: Activity has become a proxy for value.
value.move: Trace work all the way to the customer or business outcome.
value.ask: If we stopped doing this, who would actually lose value?

incentives.name: Incentives
incentives.tag: Look at what the system actually rewards.
incentives.healthy: The behaviors that get rewarded are broadly aligned with what the organization says it values.
incentives.warning: People optimize metrics, protect their territory, avoid risk, or pursue short-term wins despite the stated strategy.
incentives.pattern: The real strategy is being communicated through consequences, not words.
incentives.move: Examine what gets rewarded, promoted, measured, celebrated, and tolerated.
incentives.ask: What behavior are we unintentionally paying people to produce?

leverage.name: Leverage
leverage.healthy: A decision, process improvement, relationship, or coaching intervention improves outcomes far beyond the initial effort.
leverage.warning: Leaders are busy everywhere but progress is slow. More people and more effort aren't producing proportional results.
leverage.pattern: Effort is being applied to symptoms instead of constraints or high-leverage points.
leverage.move: Find the point where changing one thing changes many things.
leverage.ask: Where would one hour of attention create the greatest downstream impact?

rescue.name: Rescuing
rescue.coach: You step in and fix it, or give the answer before you have asked. It works today and teaches the team to wait for you.

avoid.name: Avoiding
avoid.coach: You wait, soften, or hand it off. The conversation you skip is usually the one that matters.

control.name: Controlling
control.coach: You reach for a rule, a check or a consequence where a conversation would do.

please.name: Pleasing
please.coach: You protect how people feel about you, or decide what they can handle.

promise.name: Over-promising
promise.coach: You commit, or cheer a commitment, past what the evidence supports.

blame.name: Defending
blame.coach: You explain or point elsewhere before saying what is yours.

grind.name: Grinding
grind.coach: You answer pressure with more hours and call it dedication.

narrow.name: One explanation
narrow.coach: You settle on the first story that fits and stop looking.

standard.name: Standards
standard.blurb: Say what good looks like, and hold it for everyone.
standard.strong: You set the bar in plain words and hold it, including for people you like.
standard.watch: You let a standard bend for people you like or numbers you need.

candor.name: Candor
candor.blurb: Say the true thing, early, and kindly.
candor.strong: You say the hard thing early and plainly, and stay kind.
candor.watch: You soften or delay the hard thing until it is harder.

system.name: Systems
system.blurb: Build it so results don't depend on a hero.
system.strong: You fix the process, not just the problem.
system.watch: You fix it yourself, or lean on the one person who delivers.

trust.name: Trust and verify
trust.blurb: Give trust freely. Check what matters, the same way for everyone.
trust.strong: You trust the person and check the work, and say so.
trust.watch: You take confidence for evidence, or check people in ways they feel.

self.name: Leading yourself
self.blurb: Own your reactions, your fears and your rest.
self.strong: You name your part first and protect the rest you need.
self.watch: You defend, push through, or hold on to the work you love.

across.name: Up and across
across.blurb: Carry the truth up, the context down, and a fair view sideways.
across.strong: You bring the range, the drivers and the ask.
across.watch: You promise upward, stay quiet across, or see only your own function.

grow.name: Growing people
grow.blurb: Ask first. Help them get better, not just get it done.
grow.strong: You ask before you answer and stay beside people as they decide.
grow.watch: You answer fast, rescue, or take the quiet for the answer.

lens.lesson: Give honest feedback and build trust.

tension.lesson: Useful metrics keep misses visible.

cases.pause: Who should tell Dana: you now, or your director in January?
cases.principle: Delayed kindness is a loan she repays with interest.
cases.next_move: Compare commit and actual for every rep. Book the talk.
cases.strong_move: Walk her through her three quarters, side by side.

lens.lesson: Clear expectations matter more than one person's results.

tension.lesson: Honest feedback only works inside trust.

cases.pause: What will the team learn from your next move?
cases.principle: What you allow in your best rep becomes everyone's rule.
cases.next_move: Walk three “executed” displays you haven't seen.
cases.strong_move: Tell Marcus today the rule is the same for everyone.

lens.lesson: Effective processes start from clear expectations and a measure someone uses.

tension.lesson: Give people context to decide.

cases.pause: Could you explain this rule, or only enforce it?
cases.principle: A standard with a reason survives its first bad Friday.
cases.next_move: Pick one inherited routine. Cut every unused field.
cases.strong_move: Say what the report is for, and cut it to three fields.

lens.lesson: Fix the process, not just the one exception.

tension.lesson: Autonomy and context let strong people act.

cases.pause: Would your answer change for a middle performer?
cases.principle: A rule only your best person can skip is a perk.
cases.next_move: Ask each rep: what is Monday's call for?
cases.strong_move: Rebuild the call around one real problem first.

lens.lesson: Ask good questions and build trust before deciding what is wrong.

tension.lesson: Stay curious; your story may be a reaction.

cases.pause: What would Ray want you to ask him?
cases.principle: Say what you've seen, then ask what's changed.
cases.next_move: Book a long lunch with the person who changed.
cases.strong_move: Take Ray to lunch and ask what's changed.

lens.lesson: Stay curious and own your reaction before you assume.

tension.lesson: Transparency helps a team decide together.

cases.pause: What do you know Tom needs, and what do you assume?
cases.principle: Ask what someone needs before deciding what's kind.
cases.next_move: Learn today what leave and flexible-schedule options exist.
cases.strong_move: Ask Tom what he needs, before you plan around him.

lens.lesson: Notice guilt and ego in your reactions before you act.

tension.lesson: Honest feedback builds trust, even between friends.

cases.pause: Which costs more: some friendship, or the team's belief you're fair?
cases.principle: How you hold a friend to a rule shows your word's worth.
cases.next_move: List the three people you go easiest on. Book one talk.
cases.strong_move: Meet privately and name the lateness and the jokes.

lens.lesson: Give honest feedback and build trust.

tension.book: What the CEO Wants You to Know
tension.lesson: Know how the other side makes money.

cases.pause: What do you owe someone you depend on and underpay?
cases.principle: Be honest soonest with those you depend on most.
cases.next_move: Learn what's on your key distributor reps' plates first.
cases.strong_move: Call Mike and ask what's behind the two misses.

lens.lesson: Give honest feedback and help talented people grow.

tension.lesson: Take responsibility for your part.

cases.pause: What did Lena hear in “next cycle”? What did you mean?
cases.principle: A vague promise is a debt. Pay it with specifics.
cases.next_move: List every “next cycle” you've said. Make each a date or a no.
cases.strong_move: Tell her now: not this cycle, and here's why.

lens.lesson: Strong outcomes shouldn't depend on one person rescuing a broken process.

tension.lesson: Helping people perform can mean being slower today.

cases.pause: Whose proposal is this, and what does the team learn?
cases.principle: Weekly fixes are a process problem, not a favor.
cases.next_move: List the last five things you fixed. Write a checklist for the commonest.
cases.strong_move: Sit with her at the keyboard and fix this one together.

lens.lesson: Strong outcomes shouldn't depend on one person.

tension.lesson: Trust built over years earns the right to ask for more.

cases.pause: Is it loyal to leave him carrying this alone?
cases.principle: One-person dependence isn't loyalty. It's a risk he carries alone.
cases.next_move: List your five biggest accounts and who else could run each.
cases.strong_move: Ask Sam to design his own backup, starting with why.

lens.book: What the CEO Wants You to Know
lens.lesson: Know what drives profit and cash before celebrating a number.

tension.lesson: Pay shapes behavior; bring psychology and economics.

cases.pause: What does telling your director now risk, and what does waiting risk?
cases.principle: People do what the number pays for. Fix yours first.
cases.next_move: For each number you pay on, ask how a clever rep could game it.
cases.strong_move: Ask your director to pay you on retail, not shipments.

lens.lesson: Give people context to decide without waiting for permission.

tension.lesson: Useful metrics let you check what was decided.

cases.pause: What are you protecting by approving $900?
cases.principle: Give context and a limit, not permission case by case.
cases.next_move: Ask a rep what they skipped for fear of not being allowed.
cases.strong_move: Give everyone the budget and a $2,000 limit.

lens.lesson: Ask good questions and give honest feedback, so the truth reaches you.

tension.lesson: Clear expectations and useful metrics apply to everyone.

cases.pause: Can you check his work without him hearing that you doubt him?
cases.principle: Trust the person, check the work, check everyone alike.
cases.next_move: Pick one status you accept on someone's word. Spot-check it.
cases.strong_move: Visit two stores and ask which were hardest.

lens.lesson: Statistics and incentives keep a confident story from passing as the whole picture.

tension.lesson: Building trust helps talented people do their best.

cases.pause: Would Dave bet his own money on it?
cases.principle: Confidence is a feeling. Evidence is what the buyer did.
cases.next_move: Tally each rep's “locks” against closes. Show them quarterly.
cases.strong_move: Count Safeway at half until the buyer sets a date.

lens.lesson: Build an environment where speaking up is safe.

tension.lesson: More perspectives keep you from missing the whole picture.

cases.pause: What does disagreeing with you cost a rep?
cases.principle: Silence isn't agreement. Ask what disagreeing with you costs.
cases.next_move: Ask “what's the weakest part of this plan?” and wait.
cases.strong_move: Reopen the plan by owning how you cut off pushback.

lens.lesson: Check economics, incentives and behavior before settling on a story about a person.

tension.lesson: Stay curious; notice when ego writes the story.

cases.pause: What would you see if it weren't effort?
cases.principle: Before you explain a person, rule out the situation.
cases.next_move: When numbers move, list three causes that aren't the person.
cases.strong_move: Check her numbers against the re-cut and pay plan.

lens.lesson: How you show up while getting results matters as much as the results.

tension.lesson: A team with context can carry some of the load.

cases.pause: What would you tell a friend running on five hours' sleep?
cases.principle: Tired is a business risk. Protect rest like a key account.
cases.next_move: Block next week's non-negotiables first: sleep, one evening, one meal.
cases.strong_move: Sleep seven hours a night until the 31st.

lens.lesson: Take responsibility, and notice when defensiveness drives you.

tension.lesson: A good leader welcomes honest feedback.

cases.pause: What would your best rep say first?
cases.principle: Own it in one sentence before you explain it.
cases.next_move: Write the one sentence you'd say after a miss.
cases.strong_move: Say: “I championed this program, and it missed.”

lens.lesson: A manager creates leverage by developing the people around them.

tension.lesson: How you show up matters; notice what drives you.

cases.pause: Who pays when your hours go to what you love?
cases.principle: Keep what you love, and use it to make someone better.
cases.next_move: Book the two overdue one-on-ones first.
cases.strong_move: Keep one store morning a month, with a rep leading.

lens.lesson: Give people context and autonomy so they act without permission.

tension.lesson: Notice whether your reaction serves the work or your ego.

cases.pause: If you never replied, who would decide?
cases.principle: Rest works when the team knows who decides.
cases.next_move: Before time off, write who decides what and who covers.
cases.strong_move: Reply once: “Inside your limit. Your call.”

lens.lesson: More perspectives and statistics keep a familiar pattern from passing as the whole picture.

tension.lesson: Ask good questions so the team can improve the plan.

cases.pause: What would show you were wrong in 30 days?
cases.principle: When you're most sure, look hardest for how you're wrong.
cases.next_move: Before a big plan, write what you'd see in 30 days if wrong.
cases.strong_move: Pilot 15% of effort in three markets for six weeks.

lens.lesson: Stay curious and own your reaction.

tension.lesson: Context helps people decide, and a request's purpose is context.

cases.pause: What is the deadline for? Do you know?
cases.principle: Ask what a deadline is for before giving up a weekend.
cases.next_move: When a deadline lands late, ask what decision it supports.
cases.strong_move: Reply: “What decision does Monday make?”

lens.book: What the CEO Wants You to Know
lens.lesson: Know the drivers behind your number: customers, cash, margin.

tension.lesson: Notice fear or defensiveness before it writes your answer.

cases.pause: What would your VP want to know, and when?
cases.principle: Bad news worsens weekly. Bring the range, the drivers, the ask.
cases.next_move: Write today's honest range and its drivers. Send it first.
cases.strong_move: Give her your honest range now: likely 94, best 96.

lens.lesson: Transparency is part of the environment you create.

tension.lesson: Think through what each person will do when they hear it.

cases.pause: Will they remember what you said, or that you said it?
cases.principle: Say what you can and can't. Never say what isn't so.
cases.next_move: Write three sentences: what you can say, can't, and when you'll update.
cases.strong_move: Say you can't confirm it, and will tell them when you can.

lens.book: What the CEO Wants You to Know
lens.lesson: Judge a win by what it does to margin, cash and other functions.

tension.lesson: Share context early so affected people can decide with you.

cases.pause: Whose call is it which one runs?
cases.principle: A win that costs another team isn't yet the company's win.
cases.next_move: Before closing a big deal, ask who else needs what it uses.
cases.strong_move: Bring supply chain and West's lead to one table.

lens.lesson: Help talented people do their best by asking and staying beside them.

tension.lesson: Clear expectations keep outcomes from depending on one person.

cases.pause: Whose call is this, and who learns most from it?
cases.principle: Whoever made the promise fixes it, with you beside them.
cases.next_move: Write three questions to ask before promising a date or display.
cases.strong_move: Have Jamal call the buyer himself, with you sitting in.

lens.lesson: Good questions and real attention show what is going on with people.

tension.lesson: Stay curious about what you have avoided asking.

cases.pause: What haven't you asked because you fear the answer?
cases.principle: A rep who says “fine” five times is telling you something.
cases.next_move: Ask a rep you've only asked “how are you?”: “What's the least fun part of your week?”
cases.strong_move: Ask her what's behind her question about moving.

lens.lesson: Lead by asking good questions, not by having every answer.

tension.lesson: Develop people so your time reaches further.

cases.pause: Which would Ben remember: your answer, or his?
cases.principle: Ask first, answer second, and only if they're stuck.
cases.next_move: Next five times he asks, answer “what do you think?” first.
cases.strong_move: Ask him to bring you his own answer by tomorrow.

lens.lesson: Honest feedback, with trust behind it, helps talented people perform.

tension.lesson: Take responsibility for how your own reactions land, praise included.

cases.pause: What are you teaching the team about what you notice?
cases.principle: Celebrate results, not hours.
cases.next_move: Check the timestamps on your team's emails and yours.
cases.strong_move: Tell Zoe what you've seen, including your own praise.
